findings.title: Highscore/user-level exchange with apo-games.de over plain HTTP (no TLS)
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: Network traffic at game startup: ApoNotSoSimplePanel.init() line 92 calls game.getUserLevels().loadHighscore(), which spawns a thread calling ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.load() -> ApoHighscore.load() (ApoHighscore.java:141-195). Upload path: editor UPLOAD button (ApoNotSoSimpleEditor.java:287) -> ApoHighscore.save() (ApoHighscore.java:69-138). Applet-only progress sync: ApoNotSoSimplePanel.java:97/227 -> ApoHelp.loadData/saveData (ApoHelp.java:446/419, posts to PROGRAM_URL + "cookies.php").
findings.sink: new URL("http://...").openConnection(); DataOutputStream(urlConn.getOutputStream()) / DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()) at ApoHighscore.java:77-78, 86, 122, 150-151, 159, 167 and ApoHelp.java:424-435, 452-464.
findings.data_path: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE is hardwired true (ApoConstants.java:16), so the desktop build performs these requests too. All payloads (level grid, chosen username, levelname, description, move solution, applet progress value) travel as cleartext form-encoded HTTP POST bodies; responses (5-line groups: level string, username, levelname, description, solution) come back in cleartext and are parsed by ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.
findings.attack_scenario: 1) Attacker on the same LAN/coffee-shop WiFi (or any on-path position, or a hijacked DNS entry for www.apo-games.de) runs a transparent proxy. 2) On every game start they observe the victim's chosen username and level solutions in cleartext (privacy/pseudonymity loss). 3) They replace the get_highscore.php response with attacker-chosen content, injecting their own 'user levels', fake usernames, or oversized/malformed fields (see ApoNotSoSimple-02) into every player's client. 4) They can also strip/modify uploaded levels in transit.
findings.preconditions: Attacker needs an on-path vantage point (LAN MITM, compromised router, malicious DNS) or control of apo-games.de; target must play the game online (default). No certificate warnings possible because there is no TLS.
findings.validation_plan: Run the desktop client (java apoNotSoSimple.ApoNotSoSimpleMain) while capturing with Wireshark: observe cleartext POST to www.apo-games.de:80 immediately at startup. Then point www.apo-games.de at 127.0.0.1 via /etc/hosts, run netcat/mitmproxy on port 80, return crafted 5-line groups ('1' + 60 digits / username / levelname / description / solution), start the game and open Menu -> UserLevels: the forged level renders and is playable, proving full server-response control.

findings.title: Server-controlled highscore lists parsed without cross-validation; misaligned data breaks client state
findings.entry_point: HTTP response body of get_highscore.php, split line-by-line into five independent ArrayLists in ApoHighscore.load() (ApoHighscore.java:170-183: i%5==0->level, 1->usernames, 2->levelnames, 3->descriptions, else->solution). A network attacker controlling the connection (per ApoNotSoSimple-01) fully controls each list's contents and lengths independently.
findings.sink: Hand-rolled substring slicing in ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.getLevel():123-134 (layer count taken from first character, then layer*30 two-char decimal tokens consumed) and index coupling in sort():66-105 where sortLevel is sized [3][level.size()] but filled from a list built over usernames.size() (sortList.get(i), line 102).
findings.data_path: get_highscore.php response -> ApoHighscore.load() lists -> ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.load() -> sort() (unvalidated cross-list lengths) and getLevel() (unvalidated level-string grammar) -> ApoNotSoSimpleLevel constructor -> game render/logic.
findings.attack_scenario: MITM returns N level-lines but fewer username-lines: sort() throws IndexOutOfBoundsException at line 102, the catch in load() (lines 60-62) sets this.highscore = null, and the next click on the 'User Levels' menu item (ApoNotSoSimplePanel.setUserGame, line 161 -> getLevel line 112) dereferences the null field, throwing NullPointerException into the AWT event thread; the user-level feature stays broken for the session. Alternatively a truncated level token stream aborts parsing (caught by catch(Throwable) at line 148, returning null) so a hostile server can selectively make user levels unusable. Impact is confined to client-side denial of service / feature breakage - no memory unsafety, and instruction strings are drawn via Graphics.drawString (ApoNotSoSimpleLevel.java:386), not interpreted.
findings.preconditions: On-path attacker or malicious server per ApoNotSoSimple-01; victim opens the UserLevels menu after startup fetch.
findings.validation_plan: Proxy get_highscore.php and reply with 10 groups where the username lines are omitted (only 50 lines total, i%5 mapping skewed). Launch the game, click 'UserLevels': console shows java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.sort line 102 followed by NullPointerException from getLevel, and the menu does nothing - confirming the path end-to-end.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unsigned level/solution submission to save_highscore.php
findings.entry_point: The public HTTP endpoint http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php, whose request format is fully specified by the client code (ApoHighscore.save, lines 69-138, invoked from ApoNotSoSimpleEditor.java:287).
findings.sink: printout.writeBytes(content) (line 118) sends attacker-arbitrary levelname/username/description/solution/level tuples with no authentication token, no nonce, and no signature; the MD5 helper that exists for such checks (ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, ApoHelp.java:301-310) has zero callers in this variant (verified by grep).
findings.data_path: Any HTTP client -> POST form body matching the five documented parameters -> server-side highscore store -> distributed to all clients via get_highscore.php -> parsed as genuine user levels (see ApoNotSoSimple-01/02 paths).
findings.attack_scenario: 1) Attacker reproduces the request with curl (no game needed). 2) They submit levels attributed to arbitrary usernames (impersonation of other players), flood the shared pool with garbage or hundreds of entries, or publish 'solution' strings that never solve the posted level to troll solvers. 3) Every downstream client ingests this as trusted content. This is a design-level trust problem evidenced by the client: the protocol has no integrity mechanism whatsoever.
findings.preconditions: save_highscore.php still deployed and reachable (the apo-games.de host was live historically); attacker needs only outbound internet access.
findings.validation_plan: curl -X POST http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php -d 'levelname=audit&username=SpoofedUser&description=x&solution=lrl&level=1' + 60 two-digit tile codes matching the encoding built at ApoHighscore.java:88-99 (layer digit + 30 zero-padded byte values per layer). Then launch the game and check whether the forged entry appears under UserLevels. If the host is offline, validate the format offline by feeding the same body through a local mock and confirming the client accepts it.

findings.title: Remote/local class loading capability (URLClassLoader + newInstance) present but unreferenced dead code
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: grep across all 57 files finds no instantiation of ApoClassLoader and no caller of getFileChooser() (apoNotSoSimple/ApoNotSoSimpleComponent.java:66-73, a vestigial JFileChooser filtered to '.class' files 'to load an ai'). The path/classname come solely from the constructor arguments (lines 19-22).
findings.sink: cl.loadClass(...) followed by c.newInstance() (lines 73-75): instantiating an attacker-chosen class executes its static initializer and no-arg constructor with full privileges of the JVM.
findings.data_path: Hypothetical only: caller -> new ApoClassLoader(path, classname).getMyClass(). If path is a file:// directory (non-applet branch, line 66) classes are loaded from disk; if B_APPLET (line 68) path is used directly as URL, i.e. an http:// codebase would fetch bytecode from the network over plain HTTP.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this variant: were any future/clone code path to pass user- or network-influenced values (e.g. the already-present but unwired AI-file chooser selecting a downloaded .class file), an attacker distributing a hostile class file gets arbitrary code execution on first instantiation. As shipped, no input reaches this sink and the finding cannot be triggered without modifying the code.
findings.preconditions: Requires a code change wiring ApoClassLoader (or the AI chooser) to any external input; today it is clone-and-own residue shared with sibling variants (e.g. ApoSnake/ApoPong style AI loading) where it may be live.
findings.validation_plan: Confirm deadness: grep -rn 'ApoClassLoader' returns only the definition file. Prove capability: in a scratch harness, call new ApoClassLoader("/tmp/evil", "Evil").getMyClass() with Evil.class whose constructor drops a marker file - it executes immediately, demonstrating what the sink would grant if ever re-wired.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream (or XML/XStream) anywhere in the variant; grep over all files negative
unsafe_native_call - no System.load/loadLibrary, JNI, or Runtime.getRuntime().exec in any file

path_traversal - no file write/read uses externally influenced names; ApoIO.writeLevel/readLevel(String fileName) accept arbitrary paths/URLs but have no subclasses or callers in this variant (dead shared code), and ApoCopy/FileOutputStream usages (ApoCopy.java:54-58) are equally uncalled
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens or keys stored, hardcoded, or transmitted; the only personal datum is a self-chosen username sent over HTTP (covered by ApoNotSoSimple-01)

resource_exhaustion - the custom level grammar is dimension-capped: layer count comes from one character and arrays are fixed byte[layer][3][10] (ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.java:126), so worst case is bounded; no unbounded loops/allocation from untrusted sizes

legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet entry point exists (ApoNotSoSimpleApplet.java:28 sets B_APPLET=true; ApoScreen.initApplet at ApoScreen.java:145-176) but no SecurityManager, doPrivileged, or sandbox-dependent logic is present; the applet-only cookies.php sync is just cleartext HTTP already covered by ApoNotSoSimple-01

custom binary save/replay formats (.cheat/.mar/.skunk/.defence/.rep) - not present in this variant; levels are hardcoded Java arrays in ApoNotSoSimpleLevelGeneration.java and user levels arrive only via the HTTP highscore service
notes: Path note: inside this checkout the actual project root is nested at Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoNotSoSimple/ beneath the stated source root; findings use paths relative to that project root (org/apogames/..., apoNotSoSimple/...) so they stay comparable across corpus variants. All 57 files were screened with repo-wide API greps (network, serialization, reflection, file IO, digest, exec); ~25 files were read in full, including every file with a security-relevant API hit. Key structural facts: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE is hardwired true, so even the plain desktop build contacts apo-games.de at startup; images are procedurally generated (ApoNotSoSimpleImages) and audio is always loaded from the JAR (AudioPlayer.BInJAR hardcoded true at AudioPlayer.java:19), leaving the remote-sound branch at AudioPlayer.java:68 and remote-image branch at ApoImage.java:91 unreachable. Dead clone-and-own infrastructure in this variant: ApoClassLoader, ApoIO (no subclass), ApoCopy, ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, and the AI class-file JFileChooser - all defined, none referenced, which is precisely the material sibling variants wire up; worth tracking how many of those become reachable elsewhere. The genuinely live attack surface is small and entirely HTTP-mediated: startup highscore fetch, editor upload, and (applet-only) progress cookie.
